hooks: When your interview brain deletes your entire career.
POV: you know the work. The interview decides otherwise.
I have years of AI workflow experience and zero ability to explain it on a Zoom call.
The job is one thing. Explaining the job in an interview is a separate sport.
My resume can talk. My mouth in a live interview cannot.
coreAngle: Marketing/AI operator who can DO the work but freezes when asked to package it in a live interview. ParakeetAI = the live-answer layer that closes the gap between knowing it and saying it cleanly.

scriptDraft.line: When your interview brain deletes your entire career — yeah, this happens.
I work in marketing-ops and AI workflows. I can ship a campaign, wire a workflow, ship a deliverable. Ask me to explain it under pressure on Zoom? Brain offline.
Interviews aren't really about whether you can do the job. They're about whether you can package the job into a clean two-minute answer while five people stare at you.

So I've been using ParakeetAI — a real-time AI interview assistant. It listens to the question and feeds me a resume-tailored answer outline live, in the call. [Screen-overlay: Parakeet panel surfacing a STAR-format answer.]
Not 'cheat the interview'. More like: I already know the work. Parakeet just keeps me from rambling when the cortisol kicks in.
Link in bio if you're in the interview cycle and you've also had the moment where your résumé could talk and you couldn't.

Marketing-ops background = credibility, not the lead. Story leads.
